description:
Measured on develop e515ae314 (AOT) with Process.heap_alloc_stats(): walking a 10,000-byte binary with <<_c, r :: binary>> costs 12 allocations and 544 heap bytes per step (10 structs, 2 views); a 5-clause walk shaped like JSON.string/2 costs 21 allocations and 864 bytes. JSON.decode! of one 172-byte log line makes 4,558 allocations and 177,376 heap bytes (2,831 structs); the decoded map is 1,344 bytes. By hand a step needs at most one 32-byte view of the rest.

Causes: (1) the reader is a heap struct and every fz_bs_read_field allocates a new reader and a result struct (runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs); (2) each pattern is read twice, once by clause dispatch (jobs/native.rs bitstring dispatch node) and again by the body's BackendStep::BitstringInit/BitstringRead; (3) a clause that fails still builds its rest binary.

Effect: the built distiller spends 87% of its time collecting this garbage: 16,000 lines of a compile log take 13 s.

Proposal page: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.183.html (steps, predictions, removal ledger). Probes: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz-xxd13-build/d6960461-b7a2-4585-a9e7-9f2477e57ee2/scratchpad/slow (s1-s4.fz, w1-w4.fz, dec.fz, m.py).
title: A binary pattern match allocates nothing per field read
